name: Crime and Punishment
summary: In Darkshire, Crime and Punishment begins with a sentence the capital has overturned. Councilman Millstipe seeks Dextren Ward, held in the Stormwind Stockade, after the House of Nobles spared him from Darkshire's death sentence. Ward had been caught robbing graves for the necromancer Morbent Fel.

sections.title: Justice Denied in Duskwood
sections.body:
Duskwood already suffers beneath creeping horrors and indifference from the capital. Dextren Ward was caught digging fresh corpses from Darkshire's cemetery. He sold them to Morbent Fel, a necromancer.

Lord Ello Ebonlocke sentenced Ward to beheading. Before the axe could fall, the House of Nobles claimed him as an imperial prisoner. They transferred him to the high-security cells of the Stormwind Stockade.

sections.title: An Insult to the Dead
sections.body:
To Councilman Millstipe and Darkshire's grieving citizens, sparing Ward was an intolerable insult. The nobles in their secure city showed complete disregard for frontier families whose dead relatives had been fed into Fel's dark craft.

Frustrated by Stormwind's meddling, Millstipe recruits daring mercenaries to infiltrate the riotous Stockade. They are to assassinate Ward in his cell and sever his hand as proof of execution.

sections.title: A Message to the Crown
sections.body: Dextren Ward's killing is both closure for the wronged and a political act. By ordering the assassination of a high-value prisoner under the crown's own lock and key, the Darkshire Council sends a defiant message to Stormwind. If the nobility refuses to defend Duskwood or honor its local laws, the town will enforce its own frontier justice beneath the regent's nose.

faq.q: Why does Councilman Millstipe want Dextren Ward dead?
faq.answer: Ward was caught robbing Darkshire's cemetery and selling freshly buried corpses to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Lord Ello Ebonlocke sentenced him to beheading, but the House of Nobles took him to the Stockade instead.
Dextren Ward is held deep inside the Stormwind Stockade dungeon in Stormwind. His cell lies along the prison complex's far left corridor.

faq.q: Why didn't Stormwind just execute Dextren Ward?
faq.answer: The House of Nobles claimed jurisdiction over Ward for reasons it did not specify. It overruled Darkshire's sentence and angered Duskwood residents who feel abandoned by the capital.

faq.q: Why does Millstipe demand Ward's hand?
faq.answer: Councilman Millstipe demands Ward's hand as physical proof that the sentence was carried out in defiance of the House of Nobles. It also offers closure to Duskwood's victimized families.
Morbent Fel is a powerful necromancer haunting Duskwood. He animates the dead and uses bodies supplied by people like Dextren Ward in dark rituals.

faq.q: What does this quest reveal about Duskwood's relationship with Stormwind?
faq.answer: It reveals deep political resentment. Duskwood feels neglected and unprotected by the throne, and the council's willingness to send assassins into the capital's prison shows how strained that loyalty has become.

angles.text: This contract exposes severe friction within the Alliance heartland. Darkshire's struggling frontier stands against the distant, arrogant bureaucrats of the House of Nobles.
Millstipe's demand calls for a brazen political assassination. It requires covert infiltration into the crown's maximum-security prison to bypass royal decree.
As a human of the southern kingdoms, you must weigh your loyalty to the distant crown in Stormwind against the desperate settlers holding the line in Duskwood.
